instructions.name: abandon_dispute
docs: Tenant rejects the proposed deduction with rounds still to spare; the deposit returns in
full and the landlord may propose once more.

instructions.name: accept_deduction
docs: Tenant accepts the landlord's proposed deduction as it stands.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: for it. An unverified wallet has nothing here at all, so it is read by hand in the handler
and a missing account is reported as `KycRequired` rather than as a broken account list.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the attestation account's rent and the transaction fee. Separate from `issuer` so the
backend's sponsor key can fund the write while only the issuer key authorises it; passing
the same key for both is allowed, it simply means that key does both jobs.

accounts.name: wallet
docs: field — so it needs no type and never signs: KYC is granted *to* a wallet, not asked for
by one.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: Init-or-update, so re-verifying a wallet (a new level, a fresh expiry, or a comeback after
a revocation) is the same instruction as verifying it the first time. The seeds pin it to
`wallet`, and every field is overwritten below, so there is nothing a second call can
leave half-set.

instructions.name: confirm_appraiser_key
docs: The party that did not propose, phase 2: confirms the same wallet and binds it.

instructions.name: escalate_to_mediation
docs: Tenant rejects for the last time: the lease enters `Mediation` and an appraiser decides (D2).

accounts.name: dispute
docs: Paid for by the tenant and returned to them on whichever exit ends the mediation.

instructions.name: expire_mediation
docs: Landlord or tenant: past the selection deadline with nothing bound, or past the verdict
deadline once bound. The lease returns to `Active` and the claim clock resumes.

accounts.name: tenant
docs: The rent destination, pinned to the lease's tenant: whichever party calls this, the refund
goes to whoever paid for the account.

instructions.name: finalize_deduction
docs: Landlord closes an unanswered dispute once the tenant's window has passed.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: because an unverified wallet has no account here (see `apply`).

accounts.name: landlord_profile
docs: Added so a seizure lands on the landlord's own record too. Without it a landlord who
defaults every tenant and keeps their deposits showed a spotless return history, which made
the return rate gameable (A1 in the plan). Created by `propose_lease`, so it always exists.

accounts.name: instructions
docs: rent on a confidential mint. Pinned by address, and unused on a public mint.

instructions.name: pick_appraiser
docs: Landlord or tenant, phase 1: names one company from either list. Matching picks agree it.

instructions.name: propose_appraiser_key
docs: Landlord or tenant, phase 2: proposes the wallet that signs for the agreed company.

instructions.name: propose_appraisers
docs: Landlord or tenant, phase 1: nominates one to three appraisal companies by name, each with
a fee. Once per side.

accounts.name: tenant_profile
docs: account. It may not exist yet (first-time tenant), so it is read by hand in the handler.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: because an unverified wallet has no account here (see `apply`).

accounts.name: mint
docs: The mint being allowed or removed. On allow it is inspected for extensions that would
break the escrow arithmetic or disable the confidential-transfer privacy mitigation.

instructions.name: settle_dispute
docs: Both parties sign a final deduction and the lease closes on it (D1).

accounts.name: dispute
docs: Required in `Mediation`, where it is closed and its rent returned to the tenant who paid
for it; must be absent in `Disputed`.

instructions.name: submit_verdict
docs: The bound appraiser decides the deduction; the deposit is split and the lease closes.

accounts.name: dispute
docs: Closed here, with the rent going back to the tenant who paid for it in
`escalate_to_mediation`. Closing it is also what makes "one verdict per dispute" structural
rather than a flag: there is no account left to submit against.

accounts.name: tenant
docs: The rent destination for the closed `Dispute`, pinned to the lease's tenant so the
appraiser cannot redirect it. Not a signer: the tenant does not have to be present for
their own refund.

accounts.name: appraiser_ata
docs: Where the fee goes. Pinned to the signing appraiser, so a verdict cannot pay the fee
anywhere else. Must already exist: the client puts an idempotent create-associated-token-
account instruction, paid by the sponsor, before `submit_verdict` in the same transaction
(docs §4). A missing one fails here, loudly, and nothing moves.

types.name: AppraiserBound
docs: Both parties confirmed the wallet: an appraiser is bound and the verdict window has started.

types.name: AppraiserNameAgreed
docs: Both sides picked the same company; the fee is the lowest anyone proposed for it.

types.name: AppraisersProposed
docs: One side nominated its candidates. The names are on the `Dispute` account; the event carries
only who acted and how many, so the app knows to refetch.

types.name: Attestation
docs: One wallet's KYC result, written only by the issuer key. Seeds `[ATTESTATION_SEED, wallet]`.
No personal data lives here and none ever should: the only link back to the applicant is
`subject_hash`, which the backend computes as `sha256(applicant_id || salt)` with a salt it
never publishes (docs/privacy.md). The chain therefore proves *that* a wallet passed a check
at a point in time, and nothing about who it belongs to.

fields.name: issuer
docs: The issuer at the time of signing. Compared against `Config::issuer` on every check, so
rotating the issuer invalidates everything the old key vouched for.

fields.name: level
docs: 0 none (never stored), 1 basic, 2 enhanced.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: Unix seconds; 0 means it never expires. The demo issues one year.

types.name: Candidate
docs: One appraisal company a party proposed. The name is the display form; `name_hash` is what is
compared (docs/contracts/dispute-mediation.md §4).

fields.name: name
docs: Only `[..name_len]` is meaningful; the rest is zero padding.

fields.name: name_hash
docs: `sha256(canonical(name))`, the only thing two names are compared by.

fields.name: fee
docs: Base units of the lease mint, at most `deposit / APPRAISER_FEE_CAP_DIVISOR` when proposed.

types.name: CandidateInput
docs: One proposed company, as the client sends it. Normalised and hashed by `Candidate::new`.

types.name: Config
docs: Program-wide settings, one account at seeds `[CONFIG_SEED]`. Holds the mints a lease may be
denominated in: whoever runs `init_config` on a fresh network becomes the admin that edits it.

fields.name: issuer
docs: The only key `attest` and `revoke` accept as a signer. Deliberately **not** the fee payer
key: a leaked sponsor key must not be able to mint identity (docs/contracts/attestation.md).
All-zero means no issuer has been set, and `require_kyc` cannot be turned on without one.

fields.name: require_kyc
docs: Whether `apply` and `propose_lease` demand a valid attestation from the acting wallet.
False by default, which is what keeps a fresh network (and the test suite) usable before
any KYC exists; the devnet demo deploy turns it on.

types.name: DepositDisputeRejected
docs: The tenant rejected the proposal. The deposit now returns in full, through `claim_deposit`
once the resumed clock runs out, or sooner if the landlord releases it.

fields.name: dispute_rounds
docs: How many rejections this lease has now had. At `MAX_DISPUTE_ROUNDS` the landlord can no
longer propose a deduction, which is why this is on the event the app listens to.

types.name: DepositDisputed
docs: The landlord proposed a deduction and the lease is waiting on the tenant. No money moved.

fields.name: answer_by
docs: When the tenant's window to answer runs out.

types.name: Dispute
docs: Everything mediation-specific, at seeds `[DISPUTE_SEED, lease]`. Created by
`escalate_to_mediation` and closed on every exit, with the rent going back to the tenant who
paid for it, so it exists exactly while the lease is in `Mediation`.
`Lease` gains nothing for mediation: the audited, money-bearing account keeps its 218-byte
layout and the new surface is all here. There is no appraiser registry: everything the program
knows about the appraiser is on this account.

fields.name: lease
docs: Redundant with the seeds; kept so every instruction can assert `has_one = lease`.

fields.name: landlord_candidates
docs: Only `[..landlord_count]` is meaningful; the rest is `Candidate::EMPTY`.

fields.name: landlord_pick
docs: `name_hash` of the pick; all-zero until that side picks. A side may change its pick until
the company is agreed.

fields.name: agreed_name_hash
docs: All-zero until both picks name the same company.

fields.name: agreed_fee
docs: The lower of the fees proposed for the agreed company.

fields.name: proposed_key
docs: The wallet one party proposed for the agreed company; all-zero until proposed.

fields.name: key_proposer
docs: Which party made the current proposal; only the other one may confirm it.

fields.name: appraiser
docs: The bound wallet, all-zero until `confirm_appraiser_key`. Cannot collide with "unset":
`propose_appraiser_key` refuses the all-zero key.

fields.name: selection_deadline
docs: Nothing may be proposed, picked or bound at or after this, and an unbound mediation may be
expired from then on.

fields.name: verdict_deadline
docs: 0 until bound; then `bound_at + VERDICT_WINDOW_SECS`. Only a binding writes it.

fields.name: proposed_deduction
docs: The deduction the landlord asked for when the lease entered `Disputed`. It is a proposal,
not a decision: no money moves until it is accepted, finalized or settled. Zeroed on every
exit from `Disputed`.

fields.name: disputed_at
docs: When the current dispute **or** mediation started; 0 when the lease is neither.
`DISPUTE_WINDOW_SECS` runs from here while `Disputed`, and `escalate_to_mediation` re-stamps
it so the same field times the `Mediation` stretch. Deliberately the only copy of that
timestamp: `Dispute` does not repeat it, because the claim-pause arithmetic below must have
exactly one source of truth.

fields.name: claim_pause_secs
docs: Total seconds this lease has spent inside a dispute, added to the claim deadline. This is
what makes a rejected dispute *resume* the `claim_deposit` clock instead of restarting it,
and it is why a landlord cannot shorten the tenant's claim by opening one.

fields.name: dispute_rounds
docs: How many proposed deductions the tenant has rejected, capped at `MAX_DISPUTE_ROUNDS`. Each
rejection voids that proposal; the landlord may propose again while rounds are left, and
the last rejection escalates to `Status::Mediation` instead. At the cap `release_deposit`
refuses any deduction, which is what stops a landlord re-disputing every time the resumed
claim clock comes due and keeping the deposit out of reach forever. `release_deposit(0)`
works throughout, so a full return is always open.
**This byte was `dispute_rejected: bool`** in the deployed program, at the same offset
(217) and with the same encoding for 0 and 1, so an existing lease upgrades in place and
reads as 0 or 1 rounds. The upgrade is one-way: a lease that reaches 2 stores `0x02`, which
the old program would reject as an invalid bool. docs/contracts/dispute-mediation.md §8.

types.name: MediationExpired
docs: Nobody submitted a verdict in time. The lease is `Active` again and the deposit comes back to
the tenant through the resumed claim clock.

types.name: MediationOpened
docs: The tenant used the last dispute round: the number is now an appraiser's to decide.

types.name: MediationVerdict
docs: The appraiser decided. `LeaseClosed` is emitted alongside it by the shared payout path.

fields.name: last_deposit_return_bps
docs: How much of the most recent closed deposit went back to the tenant, in basis points
(`BPS_FULL` = all of it). 0 also reads as "no deposit outcome yet", which `deposit_events`
tells apart.

fields.name: deposit_events
docs: How many leases reached a deposit outcome — release, settlement, claim or default. The
denominator behind "returns X% of deposits over N leases", and the confidence in the rate:
one lease at 100% says much less than twenty.
